**How to start:** ensure consistent supply and quality; set up a WhatsApp catalogue; offer weekly delivery routes/subscriptions (e.g. a weekly vegetable box); follow food safety and any licensing rules for your product (e.g. dairy and meat have stricter requirements).

---

## Delivery and payment cheat sheet

| Situation | Option |
|---|---|
| Same town | Riders/boda, delivery apps, own delivery |
| Upcountry | Parcel services, courier companies, matatu/shuttle parcel services |
| High-value items | Pickup with inspection, or trusted courier with tracking |
| Payment | M-Pesa Till/Paybill, pay on delivery (nearby), deposits for custom orders |

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---|---|
| Not counting all costs | Calculate profit per item first |
| Poor photos | Natural light, clean background, several angles |
| Releasing goods on a fake M-Pesa SMS | Check your actual M-Pesa balance/statement |
| Overpromising delivery times | Be honest; communicate delays |
| Too many products at once | Start with a few winners |
| Ignoring tax and business registration | Register your business name and keep records |

## Practice tasks

1. Pick one product and calculate profit per item with all costs.
2. Set up a WhatsApp Business catalogue with 5 products and quality photos.
3. Write a Facebook Marketplace listing with title, price, description and delivery terms.
4. Create a simple digital product (a one-page checklist or template) and price it.
5. List three suppliers near you and their minimum orders and delivery options.

## Summary

- Selling methods: Jumia, Kilimall and classifieds, WhatsApp/Facebook/Instagram, your own shop, local dropshipping, digital products, print-on-demand, Kenyan crafts for export, reselling/thrift and farm produce.
- Calculate profit after all costs; build trust with photos, reviews and reliable delivery.
- Use M-Pesa Till/Paybill; verify payments in your M-Pesa account, not SMS screenshots.
- Start small, find what sells, then scale.

```quiz
Q: Which M-Pesa product makes small sellers look professional for receiving payments? (Lipa na M-Pesa ...)
A: Till | Buy Goods | Till number | Buy Goods Till
Q: Should you release goods based only on an M-Pesa SMS screenshot? (yes or no)
A: no
Q: What is selling products you don't stock, buying from a supplier after the order, called?
A: dropshipping
Q: Name one platform for selling digital products popular in Africa.
A: Selar | selar.co
Q: Selling price 2,500, all costs 1,880. What is the profit in KSh?
A: 620
```

lessons.title: K. Virtual assistance and remote work (ways 111–118): VA, customer support, bookkeeping and remote jobs
lessons.body:
# K. Virtual assistance and remote work (ways 111–118): VA, customer support, bookkeeping and remote jobs

Not all online income is freelancing or business. Many Kenyans work **remotely** for companies abroad or in Kenya: as virtual assistants, customer support agents, bookkeepers, recruiters and project coordinators, often with steady weekly or monthly pay. Kenya's good English, time zone (overlapping European business hours and the US morning) and established BPO (business process outsourcing) sector make this a strong option.

:::note Skills employers look for in remote workers
- Clear written and spoken English (and other languages if you have them)
- Reliability: showing up, meeting deadlines, communicating proactively
- Tools: Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, Trello/Asana, CRMs
- A quiet workspace, reliable internet with backup (a second network or hotspot), and power backup if possible (a UPS or power bank for your router)
:::

---

### 111. Virtual assistant (VA)

**What it is.** Remote administrative support for busy entrepreneurs, executives and small businesses: managing email and calendars, booking travel, research, data entry, customer emails, social media posting, invoicing, document preparation.

**How to start, step by step:**
1. List your existing skills: typing, Excel/Sheets, Word, email etiquette, Canva, social media, customer service.
2. Choose a niche to stand out: real estate VA, e-commerce VA, executive assistant, podcast/YouTube VA, medical admin (with confidentiality).
3. Create profiles on **Upwork**, **OnlineJobs**-style job boards, LinkedIn; build a one-page portfolio with services, tools and sample work (e.g. a calendar system or email templates you created).
4. Apply with personalised proposals: mention the client's need, your relevant experience, and a quick idea to help.
5. Start with fixed hours per week; communicate daily updates.

**Growth.** VAs who become **Online Business Managers** or specialise (e.g. bookkeeping, project management) earn more.

---

### 112. Customer support (remote and BPO)

**What it is.** Answering customer questions by phone, chat or email for companies: telcos, banks, e-commerce, travel, software. Some roles are with **BPO companies in Kenya** (office-based or hybrid), others are fully remote with international companies.

**How to start:** prepare a strong CV emphasising communication and customer service; practise typing speed and professional writing; prepare for assessments (language tests, typing tests, scenario questions); apply on company career pages, LinkedIn and reputable job boards. Verify any BPO before giving documents: check its physical address and reviews.

---

### 113. Chat and email support specialist

**What it is.** Text-only support (live chat, email, social media DMs), often for software and e-commerce companies. Good for people who write better than they speak on calls, or who can't take calls at home.

**Key skills:** fast accurate typing, empathy in writing, product knowledge, using help desk tools (Zendesk, Freshdesk, Intercom, Gorgias), following macros and escalation procedures.

---

### 114. Bookkeeping

**What it is.** Recording transactions, reconciling bank and M-Pesa statements, preparing invoices, tracking expenses and producing simple financial reports for small businesses and freelancers, locally and abroad.

**How to start:**
1. Learn accounting basics (or build on CPA/accounting studies): double entry, reconciliation, profit and loss, balance sheet.
2. Learn software: **QuickBooks Online**, **Xero**, **Zoho Books**, and Excel; some offer free certifications for bookkeepers/advisors.
3. Offer monthly bookkeeping packages to SMEs, churches, SACCO groups and online sellers; for international clients, learn their country's basics or work under an accountant.
4. Keep strict confidentiality.

**Note.** Filing returns and giving tax advice in Kenya may need professional qualifications for some services; know where bookkeeping ends and regulated accounting/tax practice begins.

---

### 115. E-commerce store assistant

**What it is.** Running the back office of online stores (Shopify, Amazon, Etsy, Jumia): uploading products, writing listings, processing orders, answering customers, managing inventory, handling returns.

**How to start:** learn Shopify admin and marketplace seller centres (free trial stores let you practise), product listing best practice and order workflows; offer on Upwork and to Kenyan online sellers.

---

### 116. Recruitment sourcing and HR admin

**What it is.** Finding candidates for recruiters (sourcing on LinkedIn and job boards), screening CVs, scheduling interviews, onboarding paperwork, HR data entry.

**How to start:** learn LinkedIn search and Boolean search ("developer AND (Nairobi OR Kenya) AND Flutter"), applicant tracking systems (many have free tiers), and interview scheduling tools. HR students and graduates have an advantage. Respect data protection with candidates' information.

---

### 117. Project coordination

**What it is.** Keeping projects on track for remote teams: planning tasks, following up, running meetings, documenting, using tools like **Trello**, **Asana**, **ClickUp**, **Jira** and **Notion**.

**How to start:** learn project management basics (free courses; certifications like Google Project Management on Coursera with financial aid, or CAPM/PMP later); manage a real project (an event, church project, group assignment) using a tool and document it as a case study.

---

### 118. Remote full-time jobs

**What it is.** Being employed by a company abroad or in Kenya while working from home: developers, designers, marketers, customer success, sales, data analysts, writers, product managers.

**Where to look:**
- **LinkedIn** (filter "Remote"), company career pages
- Remote job boards: **We Work Remotely**, **Remote OK**, **Wellfound** (startups), **Working Nomads**, **Remotive**
- Africa-focused talent networks and recruiters (verify them)

**How to stand out:**
1. A strong LinkedIn profile (photo, headline, achievements, skills, recommendations).
2. A portfolio or GitHub for creative/technical roles.
3. Tailored CVs and cover letters for each application.
4. Proof of remote readiness: tools, communication samples, reliable setup.
5. Timezone flexibility stated clearly.

**Payment and contracts.** Remote employers may pay through an Employer of Record (EOR) service, contractor platforms (Deel, Remote.com and similar) or direct bank transfer. Read contracts: are you an employee or a contractor? Contractors handle their own taxes.

:::warning Remote job scams
Red flags: interviews only on Telegram/WhatsApp text, a job offer without a real interview, requests to buy equipment through "their vendor" with a cheque they'll send you, asking for fees for "training" or "visa", unrealistically high pay for simple tasks, and email addresses on free domains for "big companies". Verify on the company's official website and LinkedIn.
:::

---

## Building your remote work profile (checklist)

- [ ] Professional email and LinkedIn with a clear headline ("Virtual Assistant | Google Workspace, Canva, Customer Support")
- [ ] CV tailored to remote roles, with tools listed
- [ ] Portfolio of sample work (email templates, spreadsheets, reports, designs)
- [ ] Short intro video (some clients love these)
- [ ] Reliable internet + backup, headset, quiet space
- [ ] Payment method set up (Payoneer, PayPal, Wise or bank)
- [ ] References or testimonials

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---|---|
| Generic copy-paste applications | Personalise each one |
| No backup internet or power | Arrange a backup; communicate outages early |
| Poor communication | Daily updates, quick replies in working hours |
| Taking on too many clients | Commit only what you can deliver |
| Falling for fake job offers | Verify companies; never pay to get hired |

## Practice tasks

1. Write a VA services menu with 8 services and the tools you use.
2. Create a sample "inbox management" system: labels, filters and 5 email templates in Gmail.
3. Reconcile a sample month of M-Pesa transactions in Excel.
4. Update your LinkedIn headline and About section for remote work.
5. Find 5 remote jobs that match your skills and note their requirements.

## Summary

- Remote work options: virtual assistant, customer support (remote and BPO), chat/email support, bookkeeping, e-commerce assistant, recruitment sourcing, project coordination and full-time remote jobs.
- Employers value reliability, communication and tool skills; prepare a strong LinkedIn, CV and portfolio.
- Find work on Upwork, LinkedIn, remote job boards and verified Kenyan BPOs.
- Watch for remote job scams; never pay to get hired.

```quiz
Q: What does VA stand for? (two words)
A: virtual assistant
Q: What does BPO stand for? Write the first word.
A: Business
Q: Name one help desk tool used in chat and email support.
A: Zendesk | Freshdesk | Intercom | Gorgias
Q: Name one bookkeeping software.
A: QuickBooks | Xero | Zoho Books
Q: Should you pay a fee to get a remote job? (yes or no)
A: no
Q: Which networking site is most important for remote job hunting?
A: LinkedIn | linkedin
```

lessons.title: L. Trading and investing (ways 119–126): forex, Deriv, crypto, NSE, T-bills and MMFs, an honest guide
lessons.body:
# L. Trading and investing (ways 119–126): forex, Deriv, crypto, NSE, T-bills and MMFs, an honest guide

Forex, Deriv and crypto trading are some of the most searched "online money" topics in Kenya, and some of the most dangerous. Social media is full of young people showing cars and screenshots of profits, selling "signals" and "mentorship". Behind the scenes, most retail traders lose money, and many lose savings, school fees and loans. This unit explains what trading really is, how forex and Deriv products work, how to practise safely, how to recognise scams, and the safer ways Kenyans grow money: Treasury bills, money market funds and shares.

:::warning Read this before anything else
- **Trading is not a job and not a salary.** It is a high-risk activity. Brokers regulated in Europe must publish the share of retail client accounts that lose money on leveraged products (CFDs); those published figures are commonly in the range of roughly 60% to 80% or more.
- **Never trade with money you need**: rent, fees, food, loans, chama money.
- **Nobody can guarantee returns.** "Guaranteed 20% per week" is a scam or a Ponzi scheme, always.
- **Learn on a demo account for months** before risking real money, and then only small amounts you can afford to lose completely.
- This unit is **education, not financial advice**. Consider a licensed financial adviser for decisions about your money.
:::

## Trading vs investing

| | Trading | Investing |
|---|---|---|
| Time | Minutes to weeks | Months to decades |
| Goal | Profit from short price moves | Grow wealth through interest, dividends, business growth |
| Risk | High (especially with leverage) | Lower to moderate (depends on product) |
| Skill and stress | Very high | Lower; consistency matters most |
| Examples | Forex, synthetic indices, crypto day trading | T-bills, bonds, money market funds, shares held long term, SACCO savings |

For most people, **investing** is how wealth is built. Trading is optional, and only after you have an emergency fund and income from work.

---

### 119. Forex trading

**What it is.** Speculating on exchange rates between currencies (e.g. EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY), usually through **CFDs** (contracts for difference) offered by online brokers. You don't own currency; you bet on price direction, with **leverage**.

**Key terms explained:**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Currency pair** | EUR/USD = 1.0850 means 1 euro costs 1.0850 US dollars. First is the base, second the quote currency. |
| **Buy (long) / Sell (short)** | Buy if you think the price will rise; sell if you think it will fall. |
| **Pip** | The standard small price step: 0.0001 for most pairs (0.01 for JPY pairs). EUR/USD moving from 1.0850 to 1.0870 = 20 pips. |
| **Lot size** | Standard lot = 100,000 units; mini = 10,000; micro = 1,000 (0.01 lots). On EUR/USD a micro lot is worth about $0.10 per pip. |
| **Spread** | The difference between buy and sell prices: the broker's built-in cost. You start every trade slightly negative. |
| **Leverage** | Borrowed exposure. 1:100 means $100 controls $10,000. It multiplies **losses** as much as profits. |
| **Margin** | Money locked to keep a leveraged trade open. If losses eat it, the broker closes your trades (**margin call / stop out**). |
| **Stop loss** | An order that closes a losing trade at a set price to limit the loss. |
| **Take profit** | An order that closes a winning trade at a set price. |
| **Swap** | Overnight fee or credit for holding positions. |

**A worked example of risk control:**
- Account: **$200**. Rule: risk at most **1% per trade** = **$2**.
- Trade idea on EUR/USD with a stop loss **20 pips** away.
- With a micro lot (0.01), each pip ≈ $0.10, so 20 pips ≈ **$2**. Correct size: **0.01 lots**.
- A beginner using 0.10 lots would risk about $20 on the same trade: 10% of the account. Ten losses in a row (which happens) would wipe out the account.

**How to learn responsibly, step by step:**
1. **Learn the basics** from free, reputable education (broker academies, BabyPips' free school of pipsology, CMA investor education materials).
2. **Choose only a CMA-licensed broker** if you trade from Kenya: check the **Capital Markets Authority's list of licensed online foreign exchange brokers** at **cma.or.ke**. Licensed brokers must follow rules on client money and conduct, and give you a regulator to complain to.
3. **Open a demo account** (virtual money) and trade for at least **3 months** with a written plan.
4. **Keep a trading journal**: date, pair, reason, entry, stop loss, take profit, result, emotions. Review weekly.
5. **Measure honestly**: after 100+ demo trades, are you profitable after spreads and costs? Most people aren't, and that's important information.
6. **If you go live:** start tiny, always use a stop loss, risk 1% or less per trade, never add money to "win back" losses.

:::think A friend turned KSh 5,000 into KSh 60,000 in one week of forex trading. Does that prove they're skilled?
No. Huge short-term gains usually come from **very high leverage and risk**, which also means the next few trades can lose everything. One good week says almost nothing about skill. What matters is consistent results over hundreds of trades with controlled risk, and very few retail traders achieve that.
:::

---

### 120. Deriv: synthetic indices, options and multipliers

**What it is.** **Deriv** is an online broker very popular in Kenya, known for **synthetic indices** (such as "Volatility 75", "Boom and Crash", "Step Index") as well as forex, options and multipliers.

**What you must understand:**
1. **Synthetic indices are not real markets.** Deriv describes them as simulated markets whose prices are generated by a random number generator. There is no economy, company or news behind them. You are trading a product created by the company you are trading against.
2. **They run 24/7**, which makes over-trading and chasing losses easier.
3. **Options and "rise/fall"-style contracts** with short durations behave much like **bets**: you pay a stake and either win a fixed payout or lose the stake. Over many trades, payouts are set so the platform has an edge.
4. **Regulation:** check whether any broker you use is licensed by the **CMA in Kenya**. Brokers licensed only offshore give Kenyan clients little local protection if something goes wrong. Check the CMA list yourself before opening any account.
5. **Deposits and withdrawals** through unofficial "payment agents" and peer-to-peer arrangements carry extra risk of fraud; never send money to individuals promising to "fund your account" or "trade for you".

**Honest view.** Synthetic index and short-term options trading attract many young Kenyans because they're always open and move fast, and that's exactly what makes losses quick. If you choose to learn, use **demo only** for a long time, set strict limits, and treat any money you put in as money you're prepared to lose completely.

:::warning Signs trading has become gambling
Trading to recover losses, increasing stakes after losing, borrowing (including mobile loans) to trade, hiding losses from family, thinking about it constantly, or feeling restless when you stop. If this sounds familiar, stop, talk to someone you trust, and seek help from a counsellor or a support organisation. Delete the apps and block deposits if needed.
:::

---

### 121. Crypto trading

**What it is.** Buying and selling cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT and thousands of others) on exchanges, hoping prices rise (or using leveraged futures).

**Risks:**
- **Extreme volatility:** prices can fall 50% or more; small coins can go to zero.
- **Scams everywhere:** fake exchanges, "investment" platforms, pump-and-dump coins, fake celebrity giveaways, romance scams that end in "crypto investment".
- **Exchange failures:** exchanges have collapsed and frozen customer funds (FTX in 2022 is a famous example).
- **Regulation in Kenya is developing:** Kenya has been creating a licensing framework for virtual asset service providers, and the Central Bank of Kenya has repeatedly warned the public about crypto risks. Check the current law and tax rules (crypto taxation in Kenya has changed several times; see KRA).

**If you choose to learn:**
1. Learn what blockchain, wallets, private keys and seed phrases are. **Never share your seed phrase**; anyone with it can take your coins.
2. Use well-known exchanges, enable two-factor authentication, and start with tiny amounts.
3. Avoid leverage (futures) as a beginner.
4. Ignore "guaranteed daily returns" platforms: they're scams.

---

### 122. Investing in NSE shares

**What it is.** Buying shares of companies listed on the **Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE)** (e.g. telecoms, banks, manufacturers), owning a small part of the company. You can earn from **dividends** and **price growth** over time.

**How to start:**
1. Open a **CDS account** (Central Depository System, run by CDSC) through a **licensed stockbroker or investment bank**; many offer mobile apps. Check licensed firms on the CMA website.
2. Learn the basics: what a company does, profits, dividends, price-to-earnings ratio, diversification.
3. Invest small amounts regularly in solid companies or funds; think in **years**, not days.
4. Reinvest dividends; review annually.

**Risks.** Share prices can fall for long periods; don't put all your money in one company.

---

### 123. Treasury bills and bonds

**What it is.** Lending money to the Government of Kenya:
- **Treasury bills (T-bills):** short-term, **91, 182 or 364 days**.
- **Treasury bonds:** longer-term (2 to 30 years), paying interest (coupons) usually twice a year; some **infrastructure bonds** have had tax-exempt interest.

**How to start:** the Central Bank of Kenya's **DhowCSD** platform (via the CBK website and app) lets individuals open an account and bid for T-bills and bonds directly; minimum investment amounts apply (check CBK's current terms). Banks and brokers can also help.

**Why consider it.** Considered among the lowest-risk investments in Kenya in local currency terms (government-backed), with predictable returns. Rates change with each auction.

---

### 124. Money market funds (MMFs)

**What it is.** Collective investment schemes (unit trusts) that pool money from many people and invest in short-term, low-risk instruments (T-bills, bank deposits, commercial paper). Interest is typically calculated daily.

**How to start:**
1. Choose a fund managed by a **CMA-licensed fund manager** (check the CMA website); compare published yields, fees and withdrawal times.
2. Open an account (often online or via app with ID and KRA PIN), deposit via M-Pesa or bank.
3. Use it for your **emergency fund** and short-term savings goals.

**Notes.** Returns aren't guaranteed and change over time; interest is subject to withholding tax; avoid "funds" not regulated by the CMA.

---

### 125. Copy trading

**What it is.** Automatically copying another trader's trades on a platform.

**Risks.** Past performance doesn't predict the future; top traders on leaderboards often took huge risks; you still lose your money if they lose; some "copy trading" offers are scams run through Telegram. If you try it, use regulated platforms, small amounts and check the trader's long-term drawdowns (biggest losses), not just recent profits.

---

### 126. Introducing broker / trading affiliate (with ethics)

**What it is.** Earning commissions for referring clients to brokers (as an "IB" or affiliate), often per trade the client makes.

**Ethical and legal issues:**
- Your income grows when your referrals **trade more**, and most retail traders lose money, so this model can profit from your followers' losses.
- Promoting **unlicensed** brokers or "investment schemes" to Kenyans can break CMA rules; the CMA has warned the public about unlicensed online forex activity and promoters.
- If you work in this area, promote only **licensed** brokers, show risk warnings clearly, never promise profits, and never "manage" other people's money without a licence.

---

## The safe money ladder (what to do first)

1. **Income first:** build a skill and earn from work (the rest of this subject).
2. **Emergency fund:** 3–6 months of expenses in a money market fund or savings account.
3. **Clear high-interest debts** (mobile loans, overdue credit).
4. **Long-term investing:** T-bills/bonds, MMFs, diversified shares, SACCO savings, pension (e.g. a registered personal pension scheme).
5. **Only then**, if at all, small "learning money" for trading, never more than you can lose.

## Scam patterns to recognise

| Scam | How it works |
|---|---|
| "Account management" | You send money to someone who "trades for you" with guaranteed returns. They disappear or pay early "profits" from new victims' money (Ponzi). |
| Signal and mentorship groups | Sell "VIP signals" and expensive classes using fake profit screenshots; profit comes from selling to you. |
| Fake brokers and apps | Professional-looking platforms where deposits are easy but withdrawals are "blocked" until you pay "taxes" or "fees". |
| Recovery scams | After you lose money, someone offers to "recover" it for a fee. Second scam. |
| Pyramid "investment" clubs | Returns depend on recruiting new members. Illegal and collapses. |

**Always check:** Is the firm licensed by the **CMA** (or CBK for banks)? Can you withdraw easily? Are returns guaranteed? (If yes: scam.)

## Practice tasks

1. Visit cma.or.ke and find the list of licensed online foreign exchange brokers and fund managers.
2. Open a **demo** forex account and place 10 trades with stop losses; record them in a journal.
3. Calculate the position size for: account $500, risk 1%, stop loss 25 pips on EUR/USD (micro lot ≈ $0.10/pip).
4. Compare three money market funds' recent yields, fees and minimum deposits.
5. Read about DhowCSD on the CBK website and list the steps to buy a 91-day T-bill.

## Summary

- Trading (forex, Deriv, crypto) is high-risk speculation, not a salary; most retail traders lose money.
- Forex uses pips, lots, spreads, leverage and margin; control risk with stop losses and 1% risk per trade; use only CMA-licensed brokers and practise on demo for months.
- Deriv's synthetic indices are simulated markets generated by an algorithm and run 24/7; short options behave like bets; check regulation.
- Crypto is volatile and full of scams; protect seed phrases, avoid leverage.
- Safer wealth-building: T-bills/bonds (DhowCSD), money market funds, NSE shares held long term, SACCOs and pensions.
- Recognise scams: guaranteed returns, account managers, signal sellers, blocked withdrawals and recovery scams.

```quiz
Q: Which Kenyan regulator licenses online forex brokers and fund managers? Write the abbreviation.
A: CMA
Q: On most currency pairs, what is one pip? Write the decimal.
A: 0.0001
Q: How many units are in a standard lot?
A: 100000 | 100,000
Q: With 1:100 leverage, how many dollars of exposure does $100 control?
A: 10000 | 10,000 | $10,000
Q: What order closes a losing trade at a set price? (two words)
A: stop loss | stop-loss
Q: What maximum percentage of your account is a common risk rule per trade?
A: 1 | 1% | one percent
Q: Which CBK platform lets individuals buy T-bills and bonds directly?
A: DhowCSD | Dhow CSD
Q: Are returns guaranteed in genuine trading? (yes or no)
A: no
Q: Account $500, risk 1%, stop 25 pips, $0.10 per pip per micro lot. How many micro lots?
A: 2 | two | 0.02
```

lessons.title: M. Local services powered by online tools (ways 127–132): cyber services, photography, repairs, delivery apps and hotspots
lessons.body:
# M. Local services powered by online tools (ways 127–132): cyber services, photography, repairs, delivery apps and hotspots

Some of the most reliable income combines a **local, physical service** with **online marketing, booking and payments**. Customers find you on Google Maps, WhatsApp or TikTok, book and pay with M-Pesa, and you deliver the service in person or digitally. These businesses suit people who want steady income in their own town.

---

### 127. Cyber and e-services (KRA, eCitizen, KUCCPS, HELB and more)

**What it is.** Helping people with online government and institutional services for a fee: KRA PIN registration and annual returns (nil and simple employment returns), eCitizen services (birth certificates, passports applications, business name registration, good conduct certificate applications), KUCCPS course applications, HELB applications, NTSA services, SHA registration, job applications, printing, scanning and CV typing.

**How to start, step by step:**
1. Learn the processes thoroughly (the **E-services in Kenya** subject on this hub explains many step by step), and keep up with changes on official sites.
2. Set up: a laptop, printer/scanner, reliable internet, a small space (or start mobile, visiting clients).
3. Display clear prices for each service (official government fees separate from your service fee).
4. Market: Google Business Profile, WhatsApp Status, posters near schools and offices; peak seasons are KRA returns (before 30 June), KUCCPS application windows, HELB and school admissions.
5. Offer remote service: clients send details via WhatsApp and pay by M-Pesa.

**Ethics and data protection.** You handle IDs, passwords and personal data:
- Get the client's consent; let clients type their own passwords where possible, or help them change passwords after.
- Don't keep copies of documents longer than needed; never reuse data.
- **Never** falsify documents or information (e.g. income or results): it's illegal.

---

### 128. Photography and videography (booked and delivered online)

**What it is.** Event photography (weddings, graduations, birthdays, church events, corporate functions), portraits, product photography for online sellers, real estate photos and videos, and content creation for businesses, marketed and delivered online.

**How to start:**
1. Learn camera basics (exposure, light, composition) on a phone or entry-level camera; learn editing (Lightroom, CapCut/DaVinci).
2. Build a portfolio: free or low-cost shoots for friends, a local business and an event.
3. Post your best work on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and Google Business Profile.
4. Offer clear packages (hours, number of edited photos, delivery time); take deposits.
5. Deliver via online galleries or Google Drive links.

**Product photography** for Jumia/Instagram sellers is a fast-growing niche: clean white-background images and lifestyle shots.

---

### 129. Phone and computer repair (marketed online)

**What it is.** Repairing phones (screens, batteries, charging ports, software), laptops (upgrades to SSD/RAM, OS installation, cleaning, virus removal) and offering pickup/drop-off booked via WhatsApp.

**How to start:** train with an experienced technician or a course (the **Computer maintenance** subject covers PC basics), get basic tools, source genuine parts, offer warranties, and market with before/after videos on TikTok and a Google Business Profile. Popular online add-ons: data backup and recovery, software installation, remote support (method 87).

---

### 130. Delivery and ride-hailing apps

**What it is.** Earning through apps such as **Uber**, **Bolt**, **Little** (rides) and **Glovo** or other delivery apps (food and parcels), using a car, motorbike or bicycle.

**How to start:** meet each app's requirements (valid licence, PSV/insurance requirements for drivers, good conduct certificate, vehicle inspection), understand commission rates and fuel costs, and calculate real profit per day after fuel, maintenance, insurance and loan repayments.

**Honest view.** Income depends on hours, location, fuel prices and app commissions; vehicle financing can make profits thin. Do the maths before taking a vehicle loan.

---

### 131. Home tutoring booked online

**What it is.** In-person tutoring (method 92) marketed online: parents find you through WhatsApp groups, Facebook, Google and referrals; you teach at their home or a centre.

**How to start:** create a clear profile (subjects, levels, experience, results), ask for reviews, price per session or monthly, and use WhatsApp for scheduling and M-Pesa for prepayment.

---

### 132. Wi-Fi hotspot business

**What it is.** Selling internet access in estates, hostels, markets, matatu stages or rural centres: customers buy time or data packages (e.g. hourly, daily, weekly) and pay with M-Pesa, using a **hotspot billing system** with captive portal login.

**How to start, step by step:**
1. Get a reliable internet source (fibre or business internet with good speeds).
2. Buy routers/access points that support hotspot management (MikroTik is common).
3. Use a **hotspot billing system** with M-Pesa integration, vouchers and user management (Marzley Tech builds Wi-Fi hotspot billing systems for Kenyan ISPs and hotspot owners: see our [Wi-Fi hotspot billing system](../wifi-hotspot-billing-system-kenya.html) page).
4. Price packages for your customers (students and estates prefer small hourly or daily bundles).
5. Check legal requirements: reselling internet in Kenya may require licensing from the **Communications Authority of Kenya**, depending on your setup; ask your upstream provider and check CA guidance.
6. Maintain good service: uptime and support decide whether customers return.

---

## Making local services work online

| Tool | Use |
|---|---|
| Google Business Profile | Appear in "near me" searches with reviews |
| WhatsApp Business | Catalogue, bookings, quick replies |
| TikTok/Instagram | Before/after and behind-the-scenes videos |
| M-Pesa Till/Paybill | Professional payments |
| Simple website | Prices, services, booking form, trust |

## Practice tasks

1. List 10 e-services people in your area need and their official fees and process.
2. Create a service price list for a cyber business.
3. Plan a photography package menu with three options.
4. Calculate daily profit for a ride-hailing driver after fuel, commission and costs (use realistic numbers).
5. Draft the packages (price and duration) for a hostel Wi-Fi hotspot.

## Summary

- Local services + online marketing and payments: cyber/e-services, photography and video, phone and computer repair, delivery/ride apps, home tutoring and Wi-Fi hotspots.
- Use Google Business Profile, WhatsApp Business, short videos and M-Pesa to win and serve customers.
- Handle personal data responsibly, never falsify documents, check licensing (e.g. Communications Authority for internet resale), and calculate real profit.

```quiz
Q: By what date do most people file KRA returns (busy season for cyber services)? Write day and month.
A: 30 June | June 30 | 30th June
Q: Which free Google tool helps local services appear in "near me" searches? (three words)
A: Google Business Profile | business profile
Q: Which router brand is commonly used for hotspot management? (one word)
A: MikroTik | mikrotik
Q: Which Kenyan authority regulates internet service licensing? Write its name (two words: Communications ...).
A: Communications Authority | Communications Authority of Kenya | CA
Q: Should a cyber operator ever change information on a client's document? (yes or no)
A: no
```

lessons.title: Choose your path: a 90-day plan, pricing, getting clients, taxes and avoiding burnout
lessons.body:
# Choose your path: a 90-day plan, pricing, getting clients, taxes and avoiding burnout

You've now seen more than 130 ways to earn online. The biggest mistake now would be trying ten at once. This final unit helps you choose, gives you a 90-day plan, explains pricing and finding clients, and covers money management, taxes and staying healthy.

## Step 1: Choose one main method and one backup

Score each method you're considering from 1–5:

| Question | Method A | Method B | Method C |
|---|---|---|---|
| Do I have or can I learn the skill in 1–3 months? | | | |
| Does my device/internet support it? | | | |
| Is there demand (local or international)? | | | |
| Will it pay enough per hour once I'm good? | | | |
| Do I enjoy it? | | | |
| **Total** | | | |

Pick the highest as your **main method**, and one quick-start method as a **backup** (e.g. main: web design; backup: transcription or social media help for local businesses).

## Step 2: The 90-day plan

### Days 1–30: Learn and build proof
- Study the skill daily (1–3 hours). Use this hub's subjects and free courses.
- Create **3–5 portfolio samples** (or your first products/videos).
- Set up profiles: LinkedIn, the main platform (Upwork, Fiverr, Preply, Jumia, YouTube...), WhatsApp Business.
- Set up payments: M-Pesa, PayPal/Payoneer.

### Days 31–60: Get first clients or sales
- Apply/pitch **every day**: e.g. 3 proposals daily, or 5 local businesses visited per week, or daily content.
- Do your first jobs extremely well; over-communicate; ask for reviews.
- Track: applications, replies, jobs won, income, hours.

### Days 61–90: Improve and grow
- Analyse: which proposals or content worked? Do more of that.
- Raise prices slightly after 3–5 good reviews.
- Create packages and repeat-client offers.
- Learn the next skill that increases your value (e.g. design → UI/UX; writing → SEO; VA → bookkeeping).

## Pricing your work

| Approach | When |
|---|---|
| **Per hour** | Ongoing support, VA, tutoring |
| **Per project / package** | Websites, logos, content packages (usually better for you) |
| **Per unit** | Per word, per audio minute, per product listing |
| **Retainer (monthly)** | Social media management, maintenance, bookkeeping |

How to set a price:
1. Check what others with similar experience charge on the platform or locally.
2. Calculate your minimum: monthly costs ÷ realistic billable hours.
3. Start reasonably (not the cheapest), raise prices as reviews and results grow.
4. Always define scope, revisions and deadlines in writing.

## Finding clients: the four channels

1. **Platforms:** Upwork, Fiverr, Preply, Jumia etc. Competitive but full of buyers.
2. **Local outreach:** walk in, call, WhatsApp businesses near you with a specific offer.
3. **Content and social media:** show your work publicly so clients come to you (LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube).
4. **Referrals:** happy clients recommend you; ask them directly.

### A proposal template

> Hi [Name], I read that you need [their need]. I've done similar work for [example/sample link], where I [result]. For your project I'd [2–3 specific steps]. I can deliver by [date]. One question: [smart question about their project]. Thanks, [Your name]

Short, specific, about **them**, with proof.

## Money management for online earners

- **Separate accounts:** keep business income separate from personal spending (a separate M-Pesa line or bank account helps).
- **Pay yourself a fixed amount**; online income goes up and down.
- **Emergency fund:** 3–6 months of expenses (a money market fund works well).
- **Save for tax** and equipment (set aside a percentage of each payment).
- **Invest in skills and tools** that increase income (a better laptop, courses, a backup internet line).
- **Avoid mobile loans** for business except in clear, planned cases.

## Taxes and registration

- Online income is taxable in Kenya. Get a **KRA PIN**, keep records and file returns on **iTax** by **30 June** each year.
- As you grow, consider registering a **business name** on eCitizen (BRS), and get advice on which tax regime applies (rules for income tax, turnover tax and withholding tax change; check kra.go.ke or a tax professional).
- Keep invoices, receipts, platform statements and M-Pesa statements.

## Protecting yourself

- Never pay to get work; never share OTPs and PINs; verify companies and brokers.
- Use contracts and deposits; keep payments on platforms.
- Back up your work (Google Drive) and secure accounts with strong passwords and two-factor authentication.
- Don't rent or buy accounts.

## Health and avoiding burnout

- Set working hours and breaks; online work can swallow your whole day and night.
- Look after your eyes (20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds), back (a proper chair and screen height) and sleep.
- Connect with other freelancers (online communities, Ajira Digital clubs) for support and advice.
- Rejection is normal: many proposals get no reply. Track and improve rather than giving up.

## Your commitment

Write it down:

> "For the next 90 days, my main method is **[method]**. I will practise **[X] hours a day**, build **[number] samples**, and send **[number] proposals/pitches a week**. My backup method is **[method]**. My first income goal is **KSh [amount]**."

## Summary

- Choose one main method and one backup using a simple scoring table.
- Follow a 90-day plan: learn and build proof → get first clients → improve and grow.
- Price per project or retainer where possible; define scope in writing; raise prices with reviews.
- Find clients through platforms, local outreach, content and referrals.
- Manage money (separate accounts, emergency fund, tax savings), register and file taxes, protect yourself and your health.

```quiz
Q: How many main earning methods should you start with?
A: 1 | one
Q: How many portfolio samples should you build in the first 30 days?
A: 3-5 | 3 | 5 | three to five
Q: Which pricing model gives monthly predictable income? (one word)
A: retainer
Q: How many months of expenses should an emergency fund cover? Write a range like 3-6.
A: 3-6 | 3 to 6 | 6 | 3
Q: What is the 20-20-20 rule for? (one word)
A: eyes | eye | eyesight
```

tracks.summary: More than 130 real ways to earn online, from transcription, writing, AI training, graphics and content creation to freelancing, selling and trading, each with honest step-by-step instructions, pay, risks and scam warnings.
